items.title: Russian bombing kills 26 people at Ukraine aid centre, Kyiv says
items.description: Officials say at least nine 3,000kg aerial bombs hit a southern Ukrainian village in what the president called an "utterly horrific" attack.

items.title: Copilot in deadly Florida jet crash identified in reports as 20-year-old
items.description: In air traffic audio, a crew member can be heard shouting: "We are going to crash into the ground!"

items.title: Shop freezers in seven European countries hit by cyber-attack
items.description: The temperature of freezers in several shops across Europe reportedly rose to as high as 50C.

items.title: Fighting returns to Kherson region after longest Ukraine war ceasefire
items.description: Though unprecedented, the six-day truce has done little to alter the wider trajectory of a war that continues to grinds on.

items.title: Legal challenge to Australia's social media ban to start in High Court
items.description: A rights group will argue the world-leading policy robs under-16s of their right to free communication.

items.title: Man guilty of stealing cash from farm owned by South African president
items.description: The case, part of the "Farmgate" scandal, has left President Cyril Ramaphosa mired in an impeachment saga.

items.title: Dutch police offer record €2m reward in hunt for drug lord
items.description: Jos Leijdekkers has been found guilty in absentia of cocaine smuggling and is believed to be in Sierra Leone.

items.title: Trump to remove Rwanda and South Africa from US trade deal
items.description: The move comes barely a week after Rwanda's defence ministry was hit with sanctions by the US Treasury.

items.title: Fake nuclear warning from hacked app sparks unease but not panic in Ukraine
items.description: Many Ukrainians, who have faced years of Russian attacks, did not take the messages seriously and doubted their veracity.

items.title: Five arrested after South African farmer shot and tortured
items.description: The attack on Donovan Marx, 50, comes as right-wing groups say there is a genocide of white people - a claim widely discredited.

items.title: Wizz Air flight from Luton in emergency landing after bomb threat
items.description: A Hungarian fighter jet escorted the aircraft to Budapest after the threat was received mid-air.

items.title: Ryanair says it may freeze workers' pay and raise airfares
items.description: The airline says fuel prices may rise by €2bn in 2028 unless there is an end to the US-Israel war with Iran.

items.title: Binance users withdraw $3.6bn after largest-ever crypto hack
items.description: The exchange froze transactions following the incident which has been linked to a North Korean group.

items.title: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years
items.description: Uganda has been helping Somalia battle an insurgency led by the al-Shabab militant group since 2007.

items.title: China state broadcaster pulls La Liga matches following Mbappé joke
items.description: China Media Group, which acknowledged Mbappé's apology, has not said how long the blackout will last.

items.title: France launches attempted murder investigation after petrol bomb thrown at police
items.description: There were hundreds of arrests as protesters took to the streets in cities across France for the third weekend in a row.

items.title: Popular Australian children's author jailed over child exploitation offences
items.description: The author of Jasper Jones and Runt pleaded guilty in May after police raided his home months earlier.

items.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill eight including child, hospitals say
items.description: Five officers from the Hamas-run police have been killed in Khan Younis and three people, including a child, killed in Gaza City, officials say.

items.title: Armed police start patrols in Sydney after Bondi Beach attack
items.description: The new police unit is a security measure in response to last year's deadly shooting attack at a Hanukkah festival.

items.title: University of Cambridge scientist among those who died in Spanish train crash
items.description: Marta Shahbazi was an "inspiring, talented and passionate scientist", says the laboratory where she worked.
